faq.q: What is the cheapest yacht for a stag weekend in Marbella in 2035?
faq.a: The cheapest option is the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (Tier A) at €749 for 2 hours, or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day. Both include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT—no hidden fees. For a stag group of 9–11, these are the most budget-friendly.

faq.q: Are jet skis included on any stag yacht charter?
faq.a: Yes, the Mangusta 80 (Tier B) includes a free jet ski for the duration of your 4-hour minimum charter (€4,719). This is a popular add-on for stag groups wanting water action. Other boats can add jet skis for an extra fee.

faq.q: What is included in the stag yacht charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. Spanish VAT (21%) is also included. No surprises—just show up with your group.

faq.q: How much does a full-day stag yacht cost in Marbella?
faq.a: A full 8-hour day on a Tier A boat (Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39) costs €2,299 for up to 11 guests. For larger groups or more luxury, Tier B (Mangusta 80) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours. For other boats, pricing is on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can we bring our own food and alcohol on the yacht?
faq.a: Our charters already include drinks and snacks. You are welcome to bring additional food or drinks, but we recommend checking with the skipper. Many groups opt for a catering upgrade (€50–100 per person) for a premium experience.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for a stag yacht in Marbella?
faq.a: Peak season is June to September, with temperatures averaging 30°C and calm seas. For 2035, book 3–4 months ahead for Tier A boats. May and October offer milder weather and lower demand, often with better availability.

faq.q: How many guests can a stag yacht accommodate?
faq.a: Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) hold 9–11 guests. Tier B (Mangusta 80) holds 12. For larger stags, consider the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) or Maiora 26m (12 pax)—pricing on request. Always check capacity for your group size.

data.body_html:
Planning a stag weekend in Marbella for 2035? A yacht charter is the ultimate way to celebrate, but nailing the budget is key. This breakdown covers costs from €749 for 2 hours on an Astondoa 40 to €4,719+ for a Mangusta 80 with a free jet ski. We include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT—no hidden fees. Whether you're a group of 5 or 12, here's your guide to a flawless stag weekend on the Costa del Sol.

Why Choose a Yacht for a Stag Weekend in Marbella?

Marbella offers 320 days of sunshine, a glamorous marina in Puerto Banús, and a coastline dotted with secluded coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés. A private yacht gives your group freedom to swim, party, and sightsee—without crowded bars. For a stag, it's the perfect mix of luxury and adventure, with all logistics handled by a licensed skipper.

Tier A: Budget-Friendly Stag Yachts (€749–€2,299)

Our Tier A boats—the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax)—start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day. Both depart from Puerto Banús and include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. For a stag group of 9–11, this is the most cost-effective option. Example: 10 groomsmen splitting the 8-hour day pay just €230 each.

Tier B: The Premium Experience with Jet Ski (€4,719+)

For a stag wanting extra thrills, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) costs €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter and includes a free jet ski. This 24-metre beast offers ample deck space for partying, sunbathing, and water sports. For 12 guests, that's €393 per person for 4 hours—a steal for a premium experience with a jet ski included.

Hidden Costs to Factor Into Your Stag Budget

  • Gratuity: 10–15% of the charter fee is customary for the skipper.
  • Catering upgrade: Premium food (e.g., paella, sushi) costs €50–100 per person.
  • Water toys: Jet ski rental (if not included) around €200–300 per hour.
  • DJ or sound system: Professional setup from €500.
  • Transport: Taxi or minibus from Marbella centre to Puerto Banús (~€20–30).

Best Itinerary for a Stag Yacht Day

Depart Puerto Banús at 11:00, cruise south past the Golden Mile to Cabopino. Anchor at Cala del Faro for swimming and jet ski action. Lunch at 13:30 with paella and drinks. Afternoon cruise to Estepona for sunset. Return by 19:00. This route covers 20–25 NM and takes 6–8 hours, perfect for a Tier A or B boat.

Booking Tips for 2035 Stag Groups

  • Book 3–4 months ahead for peak season (June–September).
  • Confirm group size early—Tier A boats max out at 11 pax.
  • Use WhatsApp for custom quotes on larger boats like the Ferretti 94.
  • Check weather: May and October offer mild conditions and lower prices.

For more details, see our Marbella yacht charter guide.
